questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The culture and the possibilities for social life outside the academic aspect.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy, the university made sure to give us the crucial information before arrival in Egypt.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We were picked at the airport, in the terminal, and helped through the visa process as well as with the luggage and all the way to the car, which was also provided by the university, to take us to our apartment.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The assistance was great, the orientatin days was just american, capitalistic propaganda.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy! We found a great broker through social media. Just go in the "apartments for rent"-groups on social media and make a post and someone will reach out to you.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The commute from downtown Cairo to New Cairo Campus is quite long especially with the traffic in this country, but there are university shuttles and stuff. And you will have to be aware that a lot of the exchange student community and activities take place from the New Cairo campus, so if you live off campus you might not be a as included in the exchange student community

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There is quite a lot of paperwork before the exchange, especially when you're in the Erasmus programme but i think both AUC and KU have been very helpful in the process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Both AUC and KU administration was very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful, although one of my classes was cancelled i was told in advance so i could change my plans beforehand.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Keep up with the deadlines! And if you miss a deadline or some of your paperwork is delayed, do not panic just make sure to send emails to the administrations and make them aware of the delay.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The MSA course level was too easy for us. The class pretty much just summed up the MSA we had leaned at home, so I would recommend for students from the Middle Eastern studies (arabic) at KU to get a higher level MSA than intermediate. The other courses i took was good. (Reading and Writing, Media and ECA the colloquial egyptian arabic)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I would say it is very different as it is an american school system, so more quizzes and not the same style of teaching as in Denmark but you get used to it fairly quickly.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: MSA, ECA, Media and Reading and Writing at the ALIN

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the same courses and in addition the listening and speaking, our classmates who had the programme really benefitted from it.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The phone tax! And tips for everything.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything is very cheap in Egypt. But all import goods are more or less the same price as in Europe.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I studied at the downtown campus of AUC and there is nothing there. But they have really good facilities for everything in the New Cairo campus.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of things, but I did not participate in anything.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: n/a

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Spend your weekends and holidays as a tourist! Go see all the sights in and around Cairo, go to Fayyoum, go to Hurgada, go to Ain Soukhna, go to Aswan and Luxor.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: A little hard for me, as there is very much noise and dirt everywhere.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: How time is managed.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The helpfulness of the locals.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Dont expect anything to on time, have patience. 
2. Get a higher level in the classes than you think, you can change it during the first week. (If you are here to study arabic)
3. Talk to everyone in school, in the streets in the local shop, your doorman, and ask for help if you need it.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: We were told that all kinds of things and people here i Cairo are dangerous and we shouldn't do it, like take a taxi or eat food from street vendors and stuff like that and I personally dont think that was very good advice. Take care of yourself and be aware of the situations you are in, but dont be afraid of living like a normal person here.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Simply living in another country for a longer period as opposed to just visiting for a shorter time.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Halfway in the semester I got very homesick, and I still had a long time left here, but I tried to just enjoy the opportunities I had here and to focus on getting through and now I look back and think, hey I made it.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
